cards.title: Introduction to Flask
cards.content:
Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework in Python. It is designed to make getting started quick and easy, with the ability to scale up to complex applications.

from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def hello():
    return 'Hello, World!'

options.text: A lightweight WSGI web application framework in Python

cards.title: Routing in Flask
cards.content:
Routing is used to bind a URL to a function. In Flask, the route() decorator is used to tell Flask what URL should trigger our function.

@app.route('/profile/<username>')
def show_profile(username):
    return f'User {username}'

content.sentence: To bind a URL to a function in Flask, we use the @app.____() decorator.

cards.title: Request and Response Cycle
cards.content:
Flask provides access to request data via the global request object. You can access form data, query parameters, and JSON payloads easily.

from flask import request

@app.route('/login', methods=['POST'])
def login():
    username = request.form['username']
    return f'Welcome {username}'

pairs.right: Sends user to a different URL

steps: Client sends HTTP request to the Flask server
Flask matches the URL path to a registered route function
The view function executes and processes the logic
Flask returns the HTTP response back to the client

cards.title: Templates with Jinja2
cards.content:
Flask uses the Jinja2 template engine to dynamically generate HTML. Variables can be passed from Python to HTML using double curly braces.

<!-- templates/index.html -->
<h1>Hello {{ name }}</h1>

cards.title: Running the Application
cards.content:
To run your Flask application locally, use the app.run() method inside a conditional check.

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True, port=5000)

content.sentence: Passing debug=____ inside app.run() enables the interactive debugger and auto-reloader.

cards.title: Conclusion & Next Steps
cards.content:
You have learned the fundamentals of Flask: creating an app, defining routes, handling requests, rendering Jinja2 templates, and running the development server.

Next, explore database integration using SQLAlchemy and Flask-Migrate!
